Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://amossgo-live-9sum1.squash.io
`json-c` is not a hard depenency for ACLK.
`netdata-claim.sh` cannot write `netdata.conf` as the `netdata` user because `netdata.conf` is owned by `root`.
When `netdata-claim.sh` fails it should print the error message to the user when it's not called by the `netdata` daemon binary.

When `netdata-claim.sh` fails with `ErrAlreadyClaimed` it should also update the `netdata.conf` and the daemon in-memory config with the correct URL as if it had succeeded, otherwise ACLK is never set-up. Also the `claimed_id` has to be rewritten. Practically all the code-path of a successful claiming.

The scenario is that a node had netdata uninstalled and reinstalled, with much on the state cleaned up, but still it is claimed from the perspective of the cloud.
The ACLK thread always times out during agent shutdown, doesn't end gracefully.

```
stelios

	# run as user = stelios
```

* The point about the failed claim - @mfundul will verify he can replicate the test-case and then raise a bug in product as it does not to be something that the implementation can fix.
* I will fix the thread timing out in shutdown.

issue_context.title: netdata.conf option netdata cloud is misplaced
issue_context.body:
There is the `netdata.conf` option:

```
[global]
   netdata cloud = coming soon
```

To follow the conventions we have so far, it should be:

```
[cloud]
   enabled = boolean
```

and the default should be `yes` if the agent is claimed. So, there should be no need to enable the cloud. Just claim the agent and you are done.
comments: This is not a bug and it is not something to be fixed. There is a specific reason that we have done that way. After the release it will be a boolean value, before then we must have an extra value to indicate that the agent generated its config before the default was changed.

We can change the two values from `enable` and `disable` to `true` and `false` as requested but the third value must stay for now. [Edit: this was not clear  I mean that we can move the setting into the cloud section as requested with a `true` / `false` value, but it still need the third value to be the default for now]
It is pretty common to use `yes`/`no` instead of `true`/`false` in configuration files. I find it easier to follow. Probably it is me.

I set it originally to use `enable` / `disable` but in hindsight that was a terrible choice as it is very easy to make a mistake between `enable` and `enabled`. I don't mind the distinction between `true` / `false` and `yes` / `no` - but as @ktsaou points out we have a convention.
@joelhans We need to update the docs again :)

@amoss I can put up a PR, but let me take a moment to make sure I fully understand what's going to happen before I do so. For example, in the ACLK doc, we explain how to disable the ACLK:

**Before**

```conf
[global]
    netdata cloud = disable
```

**After**

```conf
[cloud]
    netdata cloud = false
```

Is this correct?

@netdata/product please be aware of this change which be merged into the agent later this week as it will affect any last-minute tests you are running.

@netdata/infra this will also affect the operation of the local dev env.

@joelhans The convention in the code is `yes` and `no`, so the new setting will be:

```
[cloud]
    enabled = yes
```
(@knatsakis)
For the v1.22 release this will be the default value.

@joelhans it doesn't seem correct.

I *think* it will be
```
[cloud]
    enabled = no
```
@amoss @knatsakis Yes/no it is then. I didn't mean to assert a different standard, I just didn't had trouble following exactly what my TODO was going to be based on the conversation above.
This is implemented in the go-live branch.

review_comments:
When cloud is not enabled and it enters the loop to wait, hitting control -c will delay shutdown with the following message:

```
Master thread ACLK_Main takes too long to exit. Giving up..
``` 

this is because the ACLK_Main is canceled by `cancel_threads()` but then it waits for up to 5 seconds for the thread to change the `thread->enabled` to `NETDATA_MAIN_THREAD_EXITED` which doesn't happen.

We may need to use `netdata_thread_disable_cancelability()` earlier to handle this because there are sections of the code following that loop that can suffer from the same problem if control - C is pressed.

Another option might be to extend the thread state and add `NETDATA_MAIN_THREAD_RUNNING_NO_CANCEL` and have `cancel_threads()` skip those threads that will rely on `netdata_exit` to set the status to `NETDATA_MAIN_THREAD_EXITED` and avoid the 5 second delay during shutdown.

`cancel_main_threads()` assumes that `pthread_cancel()` will always succeed, and while this may be wrong, in practice `pthread_cancel()` has never failed. If cancelability has been disabled then `pthread_cancel()` gets queued and succeeds anyway.

There was a longer context that I skipped - we ripped out the cleanup handler in the ACLK thread because of the LWT changes. As a result, we need to enable cancel ability earlier and manually do cleanup in that particular thread - it is "special".

I've pushed a commit that cleans up the shutdown behaviour, could you both please check it and if it seems robust then I will merge this PR onto the "go-live" branch as I need to switch over to looking at something else (the renegotiation fix).

I've tested shutdown in:
* The cloud disabled state
* The unclaimed state
* The claimed state
* The connected state
I can't see any problems although I forgot to run it through valgrind (c.f. @stelfrag comment's above about memory cleanup).
